results.title: π-numbers (Kourovka 18.31)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\pi$ be a set of natural numbers. A natural number $n$ is a $\pi$-number when every prime divisor of $n$ lies in $\pi$.

results.title: π-subgroups
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\pi$ be a set of natural numbers. A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ is a $\pi$-subgroup when its order is a $\pi$-number, that is, every prime divisor of $|H|$ lies in $\pi$.

results.title: Hall π-subgroups (Kourovka 18.31)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\pi$ be a set of natural numbers. A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ is a Hall $\pi$-subgroup when it is a $\pi$-subgroup and no prime divisor of its index $|G : H|$ lies in $\pi$.

results.title: Maximal π-subgroups (Kourovka 18.31)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\pi$ be a set of natural numbers. A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ is a maximal $\pi$-subgroup when it is a $\pi$-subgroup and every $\pi$-subgroup $K$ of $G$ containing $H$ equals $H$.

results.title: Dπ-groups
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\pi$ be a set of natural numbers. A group $G$ is a $D_\pi$-group when any two maximal $\pi$-subgroups $H$ and $K$ of $G$ are conjugate, that is, $K = gHg^{-1}$ for some $g \in G$.

results.title: The π-core
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\pi$ be a set of natural numbers. For a group $G$, the $\pi$-core $O_\pi(G)$ is the subgroup of $G$ generated by all normal $\pi$-subgroups of $G$.

results.title: Three Hall π-subgroups meeting in the π-core (Kourovka 18.31)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For every set $\pi$ of natural numbers and every finite $D_\pi$-group $G$, there are Hall $\pi$-subgroups $H_1$, $H_2$, $H_3$ of $G$, not necessarily distinct, with $H_1 \cap H_2 \cap H_3 = O_\pi(G)$, the $\pi$-core of $G$.

results.title: Three Hall π-subgroups need not meet in the π-core
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: It is not the case that for every set $\pi$ of natural numbers every finite $D_\pi$-group $G$ has Hall $\pi$-subgroups $H_1$, $H_2$, $H_3$ with $H_1 \cap H_2 \cap H_3 = O_\pi(G)$, the $\pi$-core of $G$: the answer to Kourovka 18.31 is negative.

results.title: The Pell interpolation function u

results.summary: For integers $D$, $\alpha$, $\beta$, the function $u : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is $u(x) = ((\alpha + \beta\sqrt D)^x + (\alpha - \beta\sqrt D)^x)/2$, where $\sqrt D$ is the real square root (zero when $D < 0$) and $(\cdot)^x$ is the real power.

results.title: The Pell interpolation function v

results.title: Largest intercept norm of a shifted Pell curve
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $D > 0$, $a \ne 0$ and $b$ be integers. The intercepts of the shifted Pell curve $(x - a)^2 - D (y - b)^2 = 1$ with the axes are $(a \pm \sqrt{1 + D b^2}, 0)$ and $(0, b \pm \sqrt{(a^2 - 1) / D})$, with $L^1$ norms $|a \pm \sqrt{1 + D b^2}|$ and $|b \pm \sqrt{(a^2 - 1) / D}|$. The largest of these four norms is $|a| + \sqrt{1 + D b^2}$.

results.title: The $L^1$ norm along a shifted Pell curve
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For integers $D$, $\alpha$, $\beta$, $a$, $b$, $i$ and $j$, put $\varepsilon = \alpha + \beta \sqrt{D}$ and $\bar\varepsilon = \alpha - \beta \sqrt{D}$, and let $u(x) = (\varepsilon^x + \bar\varepsilon^x) / 2$ and $v(x) = (\varepsilon^x - \bar\varepsilon^x) / (2 \sqrt{D})$ for real $x$. The function $f_{i,j}$ is defined on the reals by $f_{i,j}(x) = |i u(x) + a| + |j v(x) + b|$.

results.title: Pseudo-greedy remainder sequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a real number $r$, the remainder sequence $(x_n)_{n \ge 0}$ of the pseudo-greedy expansion of $r$ is defined by $x_0 = r$ and $x_{n+1} = x_n - 1/a_n$, where $a_n = \lfloor x_n^{-1} + 1 + 1/2 \rfloor$ is the integer nearest to $x_n^{-1} + 1$, with halves rounded up.

results.title: Pseudo-greedy expansion
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $r$ be a real number with pseudo-greedy remainder sequence $(x_n)_{n \ge 0}$. The pseudo-greedy expansion of $r$ is the integer sequence $a_n = \lfloor x_n^{-1} + 1 + 1/2 \rfloor$ for $n \ge 0$; that is, $a_n$ is the integer nearest to $x_n^{-1} + 1$, with halves rounded up.

results.title: Gap sequence of the pseudo-greedy expansion
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $r$ be a real number, and let $(x_n)$ be the remainder sequence and $(a_n)$ the pseudo-greedy expansion of $r$. The gap sequence of $r$ is the real sequence $\varepsilon_n = x_n^{-1} + 1 - a_n$ for $n \ge 0$.

results.title: Remainder recursion
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every real number $r$ and every $n \ge 0$, the remainder sequence $(x_n)$ and the pseudo-greedy expansion $(a_n)$ of $r$ satisfy $x_{n+1} = x_n - 1/a_n$.

results.title: The first gap of the expansion of 1 vanishes

results.title: Pierce remainder trajectory
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $a$, the Pierce remainder trajectory of $a$ with respect to $n$ is the sequence $t_0, t_1, t_2, \dots$ of natural numbers with $t_0 = a$ and, for every $j \ge 0$, $t_{j+1} = 0$ if $t_j = 0$, while if $t_j \ne 0$ then $t_{j+1} = n \bmod t_j$ is the remainder of $n$ modulo $t_j$. Once the trajectory reaches $0$ it stays there.

results.title: Initial term of the Pierce trajectory
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $n$ and $a$, the Pierce remainder trajectory of $a$ with respect to $n$ has value $a$ at step $0$.

results.title: Step of the Pierce trajectory at a zero term
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$, $a$ and $j$ be natural numbers and let $t_0, t_1, \dots$ be the Pierce remainder trajectory of $a$ with respect to $n$. If $t_j = 0$, then $t_{j+1} = 0$.

results.title: Step of the Pierce trajectory at a nonzero term
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$, $a$ and $j$ be natural numbers and let $t_0, t_1, \dots$ be the Pierce remainder trajectory of $a$ with respect to $n$. If $t_j \ne 0$, then $t_{j+1} = n \bmod t_j$, the remainder of $n$ modulo $t_j$.

results.title: First step of the Pierce trajectory
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$ and $t$ be natural numbers with $t \ne 0$. Then the Pierce remainder trajectory of $t$ with respect to $n$ is, at step $1$, equal to $n \bmod t$, the remainder of $n$ modulo $t$.

results.title: A bound on when a Pierce trajectory vanishes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $a$, let $(t_j)_{j \ge 0}$ be the Pierce remainder trajectory: $t_0 = a$, and $t_{j+1} = n \bmod t_j$ if $t_j \ne 0$, $t_{j+1} = 0$ if $t_j = 0$. Then $t_i = 0$ for some $i \le a + 1$.

results.title: Pierce trajectories vanish at a positive step
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $n$ and $a$, the Pierce remainder trajectory $(t_j)_{j \ge 0}$ of $n$ and $a$ (with $t_0 = a$) satisfies $t_j = 0$ for some $j \ge 1$.

results.title: Pierce length
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $a$, let $(t_j)_{j \ge 0}$ be the Pierce remainder trajectory, with $t_0 = a$, $t_{j+1} = n \bmod t_j$ if $t_j \ne 0$ and $t_{j+1} = 0$ if $t_j = 0$. The Pierce length $\ell(n, a)$ is the least $j \ge 1$ with $t_j = 0$; such a $j$ always exists.

results.title: The Pierce length is positive
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $n$ and $a$, the Pierce length $\ell(n, a)$ satisfies $\ell(n, a) \ge 1$.

results.title: The Pierce trajectory vanishes at the Pierce length
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $n$ and $a$, the Pierce remainder trajectory $(t_j)_{j \ge 0}$ of $n$ and $a$ satisfies $t_{\ell(n, a)} = 0$, where $\ell(n, a)$ is the Pierce length.

results.title: The Pierce length is at most any positive vanishing step
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $n$, $a$ and $j$ with $j \ge 1$, if the Pierce remainder trajectory $(t_i)_{i \ge 0}$ of $n$ and $a$ satisfies $t_j = 0$, then the Pierce length $\ell(n, a)$ satisfies $\ell(n, a) \le j$.

results.title: The Pierce trajectory is nonzero before the Pierce length
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $n$, $a$ and $j$ with $1 \le j < \ell(n, a)$, where $\ell(n, a)$ is the Pierce length, the Pierce remainder trajectory $(t_i)_{i \ge 0}$ of $n$ and $a$ satisfies $t_j \ne 0$.

results.title: Maximal Pierce length
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, the maximal Pierce length $P(n)$ is the maximum of the Pierce lengths $\ell(n, a)$ over $1 \le a \le n$, with $P(0) = 0$.

results.title: Each Pierce length is at most the maximal Pierce length
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $a$ with $1 \le a \le n$, the Pierce length $\ell(n, a)$ satisfies $\ell(n, a) \le P(n)$, where $P(n) = \max_{1 \le b \le n} \ell(n, b)$ is the maximal Pierce length.

results.title: A uniform bound on Pierce lengths bounds the maximal Pierce length
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$ and $L$ be natural numbers. If the Pierce length $\ell(n, a)$ satisfies $\ell(n, a) \le L$ for every $a$ with $1 \le a \le n$, then the maximal Pierce length $P(n) = \max_{1 \le a \le n} \ell(n, a)$ (which is $0$ when $n = 0$) satisfies $P(n) \le L$.

results.title: Kneser graph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $v$ and $k$, the Kneser graph $K_{v:k}$ has as vertices the $k$-element subsets of the $v$-element set $\{0, 1, \dots, v-1\}$, with two distinct vertices adjacent when they are disjoint.

results.title: Adjacency in the Kneser graph
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $k$ and $k$-element subsets $x$ and $y$ of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$, the vertices $x$ and $y$ of the Kneser graph $K(n, k)$ are adjacent if and only if $x$ and $y$ are disjoint and $x \ne y$.

results.title: Kneser–Lovász theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$ and $k$ be natural numbers with $0 < k$ and $2k \le n$. The Kneser graph $K(n, k)$, whose vertices are the $k$-element subsets of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ and in which two such subsets are adjacent when they are disjoint and distinct, has chromatic number $n - 2k + 2$.

part.title: Language quotients and syntactic monoids
api: Regular languages are closed under context quotients

results.title: Context quotient
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $L$ be a language over an alphabet $A$ and let $u, v$ be words over $A$. The context quotient of $L$ by $(u, v)$ is the language $u^{-1} L v^{-1} = \{x \in A^* \mid uxv \in L\}$ of words that land in $L$ when placed between $u$ and $v$.

results.title: Composing context quotients
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ be a language over an alphabet $A$, and for words $u, v$ over $A$ write $u^{-1} L v^{-1} = \{x \mid uxv \in L\}$. Then for all words $u_1, v_1, u_2, v_2$ over $A$, $u_2^{-1} (u_1^{-1} L v_1^{-1}) v_2^{-1} = (u_1 u_2)^{-1} L (v_2 v_1)^{-1}$.

results.title: Accepting set for a context quotient
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\varphi \colon A^* \to M$ be a monoid morphism from the free monoid on an alphabet $A$ to a monoid $M$, let $P \subseteq M$, and let $u, v$ be words over $A$. The accepting set for the context $(u, v)$ is $\{m \in M \mid \varphi(u)\, m\, \varphi(v) \in P\}$.

results.title: Recognizers recognize context quotients
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\varphi \colon A^* \to M$ be a monoid morphism from the free monoid on an alphabet $A$ to a monoid $M$ that recognizes a language $L$ over $A$ through $P \subseteq M$, that is, a word $x$ lies in $L$ exactly when $\varphi(x) \in P$. Then for all words $u, v$ over $A$, $\varphi$ recognizes the context quotient $\{x \mid uxv \in L\}$ through the set $\{m \in M \mid \varphi(u)\, m\, \varphi(v) \in P\}$.

results.title: The canonical map to the syntactic monoid of a context quotient
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $L$ be a language over an alphabet $A$, let $u, v$ be words over $A$, and write $u^{-1} L v^{-1} = \{x \mid uxv \in L\}$. Let $\eta$ be the syntactic morphism of $L$ and $\eta'$ the syntactic morphism of $u^{-1} L v^{-1}$. This is the monoid morphism from the image of $\eta$ to the syntactic monoid of $u^{-1} L v^{-1}$ that sends $\eta(x)$ to $\eta'(x)$ for every word $x$ over $A$.

results.title: Size bound for the syntactic monoid of a context quotient
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ be a language over an alphabet $A$, let $u, v$ be words over $A$, and write $u^{-1} L v^{-1} = \{x \mid uxv \in L\}$ for the context quotient. If the image of the syntactic morphism of $L$ and the syntactic monoid of $u^{-1} L v^{-1}$ are both finite, then the syntactic monoid of $u^{-1} L v^{-1}$ has at most as many elements as the image of the syntactic morphism of $L$.

results.title: Context quotients preserve finiteness of the syntactic monoid
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ be a language over an alphabet $A$ whose syntactic monoid is finite. Then for all words $u, v$ over $A$, the syntactic monoid of the context quotient $u^{-1} L v^{-1} = \{x \mid uxv \in L\}$ is finite.

results.title: Regular languages are closed under context quotients
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $L$ is a regular language over an alphabet $A$, then for all words $u, v$ over $A$, the context quotient $u^{-1} L v^{-1} = \{x \mid uxv \in L\}$ is regular.

results.title: Syntactic equivalence via context quotients
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ be a language over an alphabet $A$. Two words $x, y$ over $A$ are syntactically equivalent for $L$ if and only if, for all words $u, v$ over $A$, $x$ lies in the context quotient $u^{-1} L v^{-1} = \{w \mid uwv \in L\}$ exactly when $y$ does.

results.title: Right quotient of a language by a word
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a language $L$ over an alphabet $\Sigma$ and a word $w \in \Sigma^*$, the right quotient of $L$ by $w$ is the language $\{x \in \Sigma^* : xw \in L\}$ of all words $x$ whose concatenation $xw$ with $w$ lies in $L$.

results.title: Accepting set for a left quotient
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\varphi \colon A^* \to M$ be a monoid morphism from the free monoid on an alphabet $A$ to a monoid $M$, let $P \subseteq M$, and let $u$ be a word over $A$. The accepting set for the left quotient by $u$ is $\{m \in M \mid \varphi(u)\, m \in P\}$.

results.title: Accepting set for a right quotient
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\varphi \colon A^* \to M$ be a monoid morphism from the free monoid on an alphabet $A$ to a monoid $M$, let $P \subseteq M$, and let $u$ be a word over $A$. The accepting set for the right quotient by $u$ is $\{m \in M \mid m\, \varphi(u) \in P\}$.

results.title: Recognizers recognize left quotients
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\varphi \colon A^* \to M$ be a monoid morphism from the free monoid on an alphabet $A$ to a monoid $M$ that recognizes a language $L$ over $A$ through $P \subseteq M$, that is, a word $x$ lies in $L$ exactly when $\varphi(x) \in P$. Then for every word $u$ over $A$, $\varphi$ recognizes the left quotient $\{x \mid ux \in L\}$ through the set $\{m \in M \mid \varphi(u)\, m \in P\}$.

results.title: Recognizers recognize right quotients
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\varphi \colon A^* \to M$ be a monoid morphism from the free monoid on an alphabet $A$ to a monoid $M$ that recognizes a language $L$ over $A$ through $P \subseteq M$, that is, a word $x$ lies in $L$ exactly when $\varphi(x) \in P$. Then for every word $u$ over $A$, $\varphi$ recognizes the right quotient $\{x \mid xu \in L\}$ through the set $\{m \in M \mid m\, \varphi(u) \in P\}$.

results.title: The canonical map to the syntactic monoid of a left quotient
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $L$ be a language over an alphabet $A$, let $u$ be a word over $A$, and write $u^{-1} L = \{x \mid ux \in L\}$. Let $\eta$ be the syntactic morphism of $L$ and $\eta'$ the syntactic morphism of $u^{-1} L$. This is the monoid morphism from the image of $\eta$ to the syntactic monoid of $u^{-1} L$ that sends $\eta(x)$ to $\eta'(x)$ for every word $x$ over $A$.

results.title: The canonical map to the syntactic monoid of a right quotient
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $L$ be a language over an alphabet $A$, let $u$ be a word over $A$, and write $L u^{-1} = \{x \mid xu \in L\}$. Let $\eta$ be the syntactic morphism of $L$ and $\eta'$ the syntactic morphism of $L u^{-1}$. This is the monoid morphism from the image of $\eta$ to the syntactic monoid of $L u^{-1}$ that sends $\eta(x)$ to $\eta'(x)$ for every word $x$ over $A$.

results.title: Left quotients preserve finiteness of the syntactic monoid
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ be a language over an alphabet $A$ whose syntactic monoid is finite. Then for every word $u$ over $A$, the syntactic monoid of the left quotient $u^{-1} L = \{x \mid ux \in L\}$ is finite.

results.title: Right quotients preserve finiteness of the syntactic monoid
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ be a language over an alphabet $A$ whose syntactic monoid is finite. Then for every word $u$ over $A$, the syntactic monoid of the right quotient $L u^{-1} = \{x \mid xu \in L\}$ is finite.

results.title: Regular languages are closed under right quotients by fixed words
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $L$ is a regular language over an alphabet $A$, then for every word $u$ over $A$, the right quotient $L u^{-1} = \{x \mid xu \in L\}$ is regular.

results.title: Regular languages are closed under left quotients by fixed words
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $L$ is a regular language over an alphabet $A$, then for every word $u$ over $A$, the left quotient $u^{-1} L = \{x \mid ux \in L\}$ is regular.

results.title: Cooperative game with transferable utility
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: Given a set $N$ of players, a cooperative game on $N$ is a function $v$ that assigns to every coalition $S \subseteq N$ a real number $v(S)$, the worth of $S$, such that $v(\emptyset) = 0$.

results.title: Null player
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $v$ be a cooperative game on a finite set $N$ of players. A player $i \in N$ is a null player of $v$ if $v(S \cup \{i\}) = v(S)$ for every coalition $S \subseteq N$ with $i \notin S$.

results.title: Efficient value
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $N$ be a finite set of players and $\varphi$ an $\mathbb{R}$-linear map from cooperative games on $N$ (added and scaled pointwise) to payoff vectors in $\mathbb{R}^N$. Then $\varphi$ is efficient if for every game $v$ the payoffs add up to the worth of the grand coalition: $\sum_{i \in N} \varphi(v)_i = v(N)$.

results.title: Symmetric value
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $N$ be a finite set of players and $\varphi$ an $\mathbb{R}$-linear map from cooperative games on $N$ (added and scaled pointwise) to payoff vectors in $\mathbb{R}^N$. Then $\varphi$ is symmetric if for every game $v$ and every permutation $\sigma$ of $N$ with $v(\sigma(S)) = v(S)$ for all coalitions $S \subseteq N$, every player $i$ satisfies $\varphi(v)_{\sigma(i)} = \varphi(v)_i$.

results.title: Null player axiom
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $N$ be a finite set of players and $\varphi$ an $\mathbb{R}$-linear map from cooperative games on $N$ (added and scaled pointwise) to payoff vectors in $\mathbb{R}^N$. Then $\varphi$ satisfies the null player axiom if $\varphi(v)_i = 0$ for every game $v$ and every null player $i$ of $v$.

path: Tumour purity, ploidy and copy-ratio algebra

results.title: Average absolute copy number of a tumor sample
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Average absolute copy number `α q + 2 (1 - α)` of a locus with copy number `q` in the cancer cells, in a sample of purity `α` whose normal cells are diploid (Carter et al. 2012). With `q = τ` this is the sample ploidy `D` of Eq. 1; with the local copy number it is `D_s` of Eq. 2.

results.title: Relative copy ratio
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Relative copy ratio `R = (α q + 2 (1 - α)) / (α τ + 2 (1 - α))` of a locus with copy number `q`, purity `α` and cancer-cell ploidy `τ` (Carter et al. 2012, Eq. 1).

results.title: Copy-ratio slope
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The copy-ratio slope `α / D` of Eq. 1 (Carter et al. 2012), the copy ratio of one extra copy per cancer cell.

results.title: Copy-ratio intercept
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The copy-ratio intercept `2 (1 - α) / D` of Eq. 1 (Carter et al. 2012), the copy ratio of a homozygously deleted locus.

results.title: Expected allelic fraction of a somatic mutation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Expected allelic fraction `α s / (α q + 2 (1 - α))` of a clonal somatic point mutation with multiplicity `s` (copies per cancer cell) at a locus of copy number `q` (Carter et al. 2012, Eq. 2; Eq. 10 is `s = 1`).

results.title: Expected allelic fraction of a germline variant
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Expected allelic fraction `((1 - α) + α g) / (α q + 2 (1 - α))` of a heterozygous germline variant present in `g` copies per cancer cell at a locus of copy number `q` (Carter et al. 2012, Eq. 11).

results.title: Rescaled purity
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The purity `α / (m - (m - 1) α)` that, together with all copy numbers multiplied by `m`, reproduces the copy ratios and allelic fractions of purity `α` (derived from Carter et al. 2012, Eqs. 1, 2, 11).

results.title: Positivity of the mixture copy number
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The mixture copy number is positive in the biological domain `0 ≤ α ≤ 1`, `0 < q`.

results.title: Eq. 1 is affine in `q`
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `R = (α / D) q + 2 (1 - α) / D`, for all real arguments.

results.title: Calibrated copy ratios have mean `1`
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If the segment weights `w` sum to one and the ploidy is the weighted mean copy number `τ = ∑ w q`, the weighted mean copy ratio is `1` (Carter et al. 2012, Methods: "correctly calibrated copy-ratio data always has mean = 1").

results.title: Allelic fractions are determined by the copy-ratio slope
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Allelic fractions are determined by the copy-ratio slope (Carter et al. 2012, Eq. 2): `α s / D_s = (α / D) s / R`, whenever `D ≠ 0`.

results.title: Purity from copy-ratio slope and intercept
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Inverse of Eq. 1, purity: `α = 2 b / (2 b + δ)` for the slope `b` and intercept `δ`, when `0 < α ≤ 1` and `0 < τ`.

results.title: Ploidy from copy-ratio slope and intercept
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Inverse of Eq. 1, ploidy: `τ = (1 - δ) / b` for the slope `b` and intercept `δ`, when `0 < α ≤ 1` and `0 < τ`.

results.title: Purity and ploidy are identifiable from the slope and intercept of Eq. 1
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The map `(α, τ) ↦ (α / D, 2 (1 - α) / D)` is a bijection from `{0 < α ≤ 1, 0 < τ}` onto `{0 < b, 0 ≤ δ < 1}`.

results.title: Positivity of the rescaled purity denominator
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The denominator `m - (m - 1) α = m (1 - α) + α` of the rescaled purity is positive for `m > 0` and `0 ≤ α ≤ 1`.

results.title: Rescaled purity lies in (0, 1)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The rescaled purity is again a purity: `0 ≤ α / (m - (m - 1) α) ≤ 1` for `m > 0` and `0 ≤ α ≤ 1`.

results.title: Ploidy-scaling non-identifiability, copy ratios
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Scaling every copy number and the ploidy by `m > 0` and the purity to `α / (m - (m - 1) α)` leaves every copy ratio of Eq. 1 unchanged.

results.title: Ploidy-scaling non-identifiability, somatic allelic fractions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Ploidy-scaling non-identifiability, somatic allelic fractions (Eq. 2): with copy number and multiplicity both scaled by `m > 0` and the purity rescaled, the allelic fraction is unchanged.

results.title: Ploidy-scaling non-identifiability, germline allelic fractions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Ploidy-scaling non-identifiability, germline allelic fractions (Eq. 11): with copy number and germline multiplicity both scaled by `m > 0` and the purity rescaled, the allelic fraction is unchanged.

results.title: Rescaled purity differs from the original purity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The rescaled solution is a genuinely different purity: for `0 < α < 1` and `m ≠ 1`, `α / (m - (m - 1) α) ≠ α`.

results.title: Genome doubling
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Doubling every copy number and the ploidy and replacing the purity by `α / (2 - α)` reproduces every copy ratio (the `m = 2` case of `copyRatio_scale`).

results.title: Nonnegativity of somatic allelic fractions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Somatic allelic fractions are nonnegative in the biological domain.

results.title: Somatic allelic fraction is at most one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A somatic allelic fraction is at most one when the multiplicity does not exceed the copy number (`s ≤ q`).

results.title: Somatic allelic fraction increases with purity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The somatic allelic fraction increases with the purity (`0 ≤ s`, `0 < q`).

results.title: Somatic allelic fraction decreases with copy number
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The somatic allelic fraction decreases with the local copy number (`0 ≤ α ≤ 1`, `0 ≤ s`, `0 < q ≤ q'`).

results.title: Somatic allelic fraction increases with multiplicity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The somatic allelic fraction increases with the multiplicity (`0 ≤ α ≤ 1`, `0 < q`).
